historical_basis.quote:
Pangu or Pan Gu (also sometimes spelled Peng Gu and P’an-ku)
(Chinese: 盤古; pinyin: Pángǔ ; PAN-koo) is a primordial being and creation figure in Chinese mythology and in Taoism. According to legend, Pangu separated heaven and earth, and his body later became geographic features such as mountains and flowing water.

statement.id: Pangu adalah makhluk purba dan tokoh penciptaan dalam mitologi Tiongkok dan Taoisme; menurut legenda ia memisahkan langit dan bumi.
statement.en: Pangu is a primordial being and creation figure in Chinese mythology and Taoism; according to legend he separated heaven and earth.

historical_basis.quote: In the beginning, there was nothing and the universe was in a featureless, formless primordial state. This primordial state coalesced into a cosmic egg over the course of about 18,000 years. Within it, the perfectly opposed principles of yin and yang became balanced and Pangu emerged (or woke up) from the egg. Pangu inside the cosmic egg symbolizes Taiji.

statement.id: Dalam kisah telur kosmis, Pangu muncul setelah yin dan yang mencapai keseimbangan.
statement.en: In the cosmic-egg tale, Pangu emerges once yin and yang reach balance.

historical_basis.quote: Pangu inside the cosmic egg symbolizes Taiji. Pangu is usually depicted as a primitive, hairy giant with horns on his head.

statement.id: Pangu lazim digambarkan sebagai raksasa berbulu dengan tanduk di kepala.
statement.en: Depictions commonly present Pangu as a hairy giant bearing horns.

historical_basis.quote: P'an Ku is pictured as a man of dwarfish stature clothed in bearskin, or merely in leaves or with an apron of leaves. He has two horns on his head. In his right hand he holds a hammer and in his left a chisel (sometimes these are reversed)
historical_basis.locator: Chapter III, "The Fashioner of the Universe"

statement.id: Menurut Werner, P'an Ku digambarkan sebagai pria bertubuh kerdil berpakaian kulit beruang atau daun, bertanduk dua, memegang palu di tangan kanan dan pahat di tangan kiri (kadang terbalik).
statement.en: According to Werner, P'an Ku is pictured as a dwarfish man clothed in bearskin or leaves, with two horns, holding a hammer in his right hand and a chisel in his left (sometimes reversed).

historical_basis.quote: His task occupied eighteen thousand years, during which he formed the sun, moon, and stars, the heavens and the earth, himself increasing in stature day by day, being daily six feet taller than the day before, until, his labours ended, he died that his works might live.
historical_basis.locator: Chapter III, "The Fashioner of the Universe"

statement.id: Menurut Werner, tugas P'an Ku memakan delapan belas ribu tahun; ia membentuk matahari, bulan, bintang, langit, dan bumi sambil bertambah tinggi enam kaki setiap hari, lalu wafat agar karyanya hidup.
statement.en: According to Werner, P'an Ku's task occupied eighteen thousand years, during which he formed the sun, moon, stars, heavens and earth, growing six feet taller each day until he died so that his works might live.
